description: İstanbul Sabahattin Zaim Üniversitesi (İZÜ) Bilgisayar Mühendisliği öğrencileri olarak KAPTAN takımını kurduk. Ekibimiz; yazılım, IoT, gömülü sistemler ve veri mimarileri alanlarında tecrübeli üç mühendis adayından oluşuyor. NASA Space Apps Ankara'da, donanım ve yazılım yetkinliklerimizi birleştirerek uzay ve dünya problemlerine teknik, ölçeklenebilir ve yenilikçi çözümler üretmeyi hedefliyoruz.
summary:
Climate change has disrupted traditional agricultural calendars. Farmers relying on static planting dates and monoculture practices face severe yield losses due to unexpected thermal anomalies, root-zone droughts, and humidity-driven fungal outbreaks (such as rust and septoria).

To address the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, we developed CropGuard AI—an intelligent, climate-adaptive crop rotation and dynamic planting assistant. Our platform integrates NASA GEOS-S2S seasonal forecasts (T2M, WET3), 20-year NASA POWER agroclimatology series (2006–2025 across 265 grid points), CMIP6 precipitation projections, FAO evapotranspiration (ET) guidelines, and Open-Meteo 14-day live forecasts. 

Using Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) spatial interpolation on an interactive satellite map, CropGuard AI analyzes a farmer's exact parcel alongside soil texture, pH, irrigation method, budget, and machinery. It breaks disease cycles by recommending optimal alternative crop rotations, shifted planting windows ("-X Days Early Planting"), a 3D virtual field phenology simulation, and actionable 14-day field task schedules—empowering farmers to save water, protect yields, and secure their net income.
details:
How It Works & What It Does CropGuard AI is an intelligent decision-support system designed to help farmers adapt to climate change. The user starts by dropping a pin on an interactive satellite map and entering their field's parameters (soil type, pH, budget, current monoculture crop, irrigation type, and machinery). The system then fetches 20-year historical climate data via NASA POWER and seasonal predictions via NASA GEOS-S2S. Using an advanced algorithm, it evaluates the risk of temperature/humidity-driven fungal outbreaks and drought, ultimately generating a dynamically adjusted planting window ("-X Days Early Planting") and top alternative crop rotation strategies.

Benefits & Intended Impact Traditional agricultural calendars are failing. By shifting planting dates and breaking monoculture cycles, our system directly prevents massive yield losses caused by fungal diseases and root-zone droughts. The intended impact is to empower small-to-medium-scale farmers to make scientifically backed, economically viable decisions that save water, protect their soil health, and maximize net income without requiring deep technical knowledge.

Tools & Technologies Used We built a robust, 3-tier hybrid-fallback architecture:

  • Frontend: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (ES Modules), Chart.js (for data visualization), and Leaflet/Esri (for interactive mapping).
  • Backend & API Gateway: Node.js, Express, and node-cache (reducing API latency significantly).
  • Scientific Engine & Algorithm: Python, FastAPI, Pandas, and Xarray/NetCDF4 for processing heavy NASA climate models.
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER API, NASA GEOS-S2S, CMIP6, Open-Meteo API, and FAO Agrometeorological guidelines.
  • Version Control & Environment: Git, GitHub, VS Code.

Creativity & Team Considerations Our main consideration was real-world applicability. We didn't just build a weather app; we integrated real agronomic constraints like a farmer's budget and machinery fleet. Our most creative feature is the "3D Virtual Field Simulation" (drawn via Canvas), which visually compares two different crop scenarios side-by-side across 5 phenological growth stages. Furthermore, we designed a hybrid-fallback mechanism: even if the Python algorithm server goes offline, the frontend's embedded decision engine and localized NASA grid data ensure the farmer still gets actionable results. Finally, to ensure global accessibility, we integrated 12-language (i18n) support.
